nodes.label: Turnover Intention
nodes.definition: The deliberate and conscious willingness of an employee to leave the organization within a certain time period
nodes.description: This is the primary outcome we're trying to predict - understanding who is likely to leave allows for proactive retention efforts

nodes.label: Human Capital Value
nodes.definition: The accumulated knowledge, skills, experience, and expertise that an employee brings to the organization
nodes.description: Employees with higher or more transferable human capital may have more external opportunities, affecting their likelihood to leave

nodes.label: Professional Mobility
nodes.definition: The ease with which an employee can move between jobs, including their career flexibility and market demand for their skills
nodes.description: Higher mobility increases churn risk as employees have more alternatives and lower switching costs

nodes.label: Organizational Tenure
nodes.definition: The depth and duration of an employee's relationship with the organization, including their institutional knowledge and investment in the company
nodes.description: Longer tenure typically correlates with lower turnover as employees have greater organizational investment

nodes.label: Career Progression
nodes.definition: The trajectory and velocity of advancement through roles, responsibilities, and hierarchical levels within the organization
nodes.description: Stagnant career progression is a key driver of turnover as ambitious employees seek growth opportunities elsewhere

nodes.label: Job Embeddedness
nodes.definition: The extent to which an employee is enmeshed in their job through links, fit, and potential sacrifices associated with leaving
nodes.description: Higher embeddedness creates 'sticky' factors that reduce likelihood of voluntary turnover

nodes.label: Compensation Competitiveness
nodes.definition: The perceived fairness and market alignment of total rewards relative to internal peers and external opportunities
nodes.description: Uncompetitive compensation is a primary driver of turnover, especially for high performers

nodes.label: Total Rewards Satisfaction
nodes.definition: Overall contentment with the complete package of monetary and non-monetary benefits received from employment
nodes.description: Dissatisfaction with total rewards package motivates employees to seek better opportunities

nodes.label: Work-Life Integration
nodes.definition: The degree to which work demands and personal life requirements are successfully balanced and mutually supportive
nodes.description: Poor work-life integration leads to burnout and turnover as employees prioritize personal wellbeing

nodes.label: Job Role Fit
nodes.definition: The alignment between an employee's capabilities, interests, and values with their job requirements and responsibilities
nodes.description: Misalignment between employee and role characteristics increases dissatisfaction and turnover likelihood

nodes.label: Workload Sustainability
nodes.definition: The manageability of job demands relative to available resources, time, and employee capacity
nodes.description: Unsustainable workload leads to stress, burnout, and eventual departure from the organization

nodes.label: Performance Standing
nodes.definition: An employee's achievement level and contribution value relative to expectations and peer benchmarks
nodes.description: Both very high performers (who have options) and low performers (who face pressure) may have higher turnover risk

nodes.label: Recognition Adequacy
nodes.definition: The extent to which employee contributions are appropriately acknowledged, valued, and rewarded by the organization
nodes.description: Insufficient recognition diminishes engagement and motivates employees to seek appreciation elsewhere

nodes.label: Manager Relationship Quality
nodes.definition: The strength, trust, and effectiveness of the relationship between an employee and their direct supervisor
nodes.description: Poor manager relationships are one of the top reasons employees leave organizations

nodes.label: Team Cohesion
nodes.definition: The strength of interpersonal bonds, collaboration, and mutual support within the immediate work group
nodes.description: Strong team relationships create social ties that reduce turnover intention

nodes.label: Organizational Commitment
nodes.definition: The psychological attachment, identification, and loyalty an employee feels toward the organization
nodes.description: Higher organizational commitment directly reduces turnover intention through emotional and normative bonds

nodes.label: Employee Engagement
nodes.definition: The emotional connection, enthusiasm, and discretionary effort an employee invests in their work and organization
nodes.description: Disengaged employees are more likely to seek opportunities that reignite their passion and motivation

nodes.label: Life Stage Factors
nodes.definition: Personal circumstances related to age, family situation, and life priorities that influence career decisions
nodes.description: Different life stages create varying levels of turnover risk based on changing priorities and constraints

nodes.label: Geographic Mobility Constraints
nodes.definition: Physical, family, or community factors that limit an employee's ability or willingness to relocate for work
nodes.description: Lower geographic mobility may reduce turnover options and increase retention

nodes.label: External Market Conditions
nodes.definition: The availability of alternative employment opportunities and labor market dynamics in relevant industries and geographies
nodes.description: Favorable external market conditions increase turnover by expanding available alternatives
